text:
Lakewood Health System reported as Todd County's largest nursing home in Q1 2026
During the first quarter of 2026, Lakewood Health System was identified as the largest nursing home in Todd County, according to the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS).
Statistics reveal the facility provided 87 beds, 23 more than the county’s average for the same quarter. Lakewood Health System supported an average daily census of 80.1 residents.
Lakewood Health System earned an overall CMS rating of 5 out of 5, significantly surpassing the average rating of 3.2 for nursing homes across Minnesota.
In comparison, Long Prairie Health Care Center was the county's second largest nursing home with 60 beds in operation, while Central Todd County Care Center ranked third, with 45 available beds.
In the first quarter of 2026, Lakewood Health System reported no fines or penalties.
Todd County, Minnesota, had two non-profit nursing homes in total.
U.S. Census Bureau estimates show the older adult population in the United States continues to rise, while the number of younger residents is declining. From 2020 to 2024, the population of Americans 65 and older grew by 13%, as those under 18 decreased by 1.7%. Over the past century, the nation’s older population has surged from 4.9 million in 1920 to more than 61 million as of 2024.
A report released in 2021 estimates nearly half of this group—around 28 million people—may require long-term assistance and support. Furthermore, the analysis indicates that more than one-third could eventually enter nursing home care.
“Living a long life is something that many of us want and could get,” said Jesse Slome, executive director of the American Association for Long-Term Care Insurance, an insurance education group. “But when we live a long life, the chances of us needing long-term care increase exponentially. But when you need that type of care, there are limited options.”
